title: Fixed-open core for gluing smallness of perfect classes
statement: For a fixed open immersion f : Y ⟶ X with opensRange f = U ⊔ V, under the three smallness hypotheses on U, V and U ⊓ V and derived-category structures on Y and all its opens, the skeleton of perfect derived quasi-coherent objects on Y is u-small.

proof.text: Set A=f inverse U and B=f inverse V; preimage_opensRange and the range equality show A union B is top. Apply endpoint smallness and the triangle-presentation theorem to every perfect quasi-coherent object.
K-injective resolutions give LocallySmall u of the ambient derived category via the source-library DerivedCategory.locallySmall instance, for the supplied localization universe w.

The proved private small_skeleton_of_triangle_terms helper encodes the second triangle arrow between chosen skeleton representatives of its second and third objects. Its indexing type is a dependent sum of the two small skeletons and their u-small Hom type. Map each distinguished triangle to its arrow skeleton; every such class belongs to the range of the encoded family. Equality of arrow classes gives an arrow isomorphism. Rotate the two distinguished triangles and use Mathlib exists_iso_of_arrow_iso to get an isomorphism of shifted first terms. Full faithfulness of shift removes the shift, and full faithfulness of the perfect/QCoh inclusion yields equality of perfect skeleton classes. This injects that skeleton into the small range of arrow classes. small_of_injective concludes without selecting an arbitrary cone object.
